data.title: Take-Two's 'Grand Theft Auto VI' Hits Nearly $4 Billion in Sales on Launch Day
data.description:
By Ben Fritz

"Grand Theft Auto VI," the latest installment of the Take-Two Interactive Software video-game series, grossed nearly $4 billion in sales by the end of its launch day, according to the company.

Take-Two said "GTA VI" sold 32.5 million pre-ordered games to customers who wanted to download and play as soon as it was available Thursday. The retail value of the sales through the end of launch day were about $3.79 billion, which Take-Two said was a record for any entertainment property.

When "Grand Theft Auto V"--the previous edition of the series published by Take-Two-unit Rockstar Games--launched in 2013, it sold $800 million worth of copies on its first day. That game cost a minimum of $60, while the basic version of "GTA VI" costs $80.

Shares of Take-Two are down slightly, at $208.55, amid a broader market selloff late Friday, after rising to $218.69 earlier in the session.

data.title: Trump Continues To Insist On Huang’s Return At Nvidia’s Helm, Threatens US Firms Building Overseas Data Centers
data.description:
Key points:
  • Trump advocated for a second chance for former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang following a scandal involving a suspected Chinese spy.
  • Nvidia would reinstate Jensen as CEO “if they were smart,” Trump said during a White House press conference.
  • Trump also threatened heavy taxes on American companies expanding AI data center capacity outside the United States.

President Donald Trump on Friday urged Jensen Huang to apologise and return to lead Nvidia Corp.(NVDA), even as the board of directors explicitly signaled no plans to reinstate the former chief executive.

Speaking during a White House press briefing, Trump praised Huang's past impact on the company and argued that he deserves another opportunity. Trump noted that he still favors Apple Inc. CEO Tim Cook as his preferred successor to Huang, while adding that he would like to see Huang get a second chance.

Trump called Huang one of the world’s sharpest minds and credited him with giving the U.S. a decade-long lead over rival companies. He said he would like to see Huang offer a “big apology” and step back into the role. He also added that Nvidia’s board should reinstate Jensen as CEO, “if they were smart.”

“I’d like to see Jensen make a big apology and go back,” Trump said Friday at a White House press conference. “He put us in a position where we are literally 10 years advanced over other companies.”

Trump Discusses Nvidia And Chip Exports 

According to Trump, Huang’s status came up during his meeting earlier in the week with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, where Trump said Xi likewise described Huang as brilliant. Those high-level talks unfolded against the backdrop of disclosures that Huang had a relationship with an alleged Chinese spy tied to a Singapore-based firm that acquired advanced Nvidia chips.

The controversy also exposed visible divisions inside the U.S. government over its China policy Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has publicly faulted the Commerce Department, headed by Secretary Howard Lutnick, for failing to stop advanced chips from reaching China.

Meanwhile, during the same press conference, Trump lauded Lutnick’s role at the center of a scandal involving AI chips smuggled to China.

“I have not lost confidence,” Trump said in response to a question about whether he had lost faith in Lutnick.

Tax Threats On American Firms

Separately on Friday, Trump warned that the U.S. government plans to slap steep taxes on American companies constructing data centers in foreign countries. The legal basis or the degree of taxation to be levied was not discussed.

Trump said U.S. businesses are free to build abroad but cautioned that they would face a massive tax, emphasizing his preference for projects to be built within the U.S.

Although the United States holds the largest concentration of computing power globally, firms are also expanding into regions such as China, parts of Europe and Latin America and India.

Major technology companies, including Microsoft Corp. (MSFT), Alphabet Inc. (GOOG, GOOGL), and Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN), have committed hundreds of billions of dollars to expand computing capacity.

Trump singled out Google over data center investments in Finland rather than directing all of that spending to the U.S., even as the company has simultaneously backed major domestic projects.

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was ‘bearish’ on the SPDR S&P 500 ETF and the SPDR Dow Jones ETF (DIA), while was ‘bullish’ on the tech-heavy Invesco QQQ (QQQ) ETF that tracks the Nasdaq 100.

data.title: Treasuries Skyrocket Amid Sell-Off On Wall Street
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Treasuries have skyrocketed during trading on Friday, extending the strong upward move seen over the past several sessions.

Bond prices surged early in the session and have seen further upside as the day has progressed. As a result, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its price, has plunged 14.0 basis points to 4.912 percent.

The rally by treasuries came amid a continued sell-off on Wall Street, with technology stocks plummeting amid renewed skepticism about the artificial intelligence trade.

A steep drop by shares of Anthropic (ANT) weighed on the tech sector following its record-breaking initial public offering on Thursday.

Shares of Anthropic are plunging by more than 10 percent after the Claude developer spiked by 17.1 percent on Thursday but ended the day well off its highs of the session.

'The IPO demonstrated that demand for AI exposure remains strong, but it has not been enough to overcome concerns about elevated valuations, profitability and the sustainability of investment spending,' said Daniela Hathorn, Senior Market Analyst at Capital.com.

She added, 'The broader market mood has shifted from buying the dip towards questioning whether the correction has further to run.'

Meanwhile, bond traders have seemingly shrugged off concerns about the outlook for interest rates, with at least a quarter point rate hike seen as a near-certainty at the Federal Reserve's monetary policy next month.

Following hawkish comments from several Fed officials, traders have grown increasingly worried the central bank will continue to raise rates in the coming months in order to combat stubborn inflation.

data.title: FormFactor, Amkor, Himax, Teradyne, and Entegris shares are falling, what you need to know
data.description:
What happened?

A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session as AI-linked shares continued to pull back as Anthropic slid more than 10% following its debut, failing to revive confidence in the sector's spending boom.

Investors had looked to Anthropic's record $81.3 billion initial public offering and Nvidia's quarterly earnings beat under interim CEO Colette Kress to steady sentiment following Jensen Huang's resignation, CNBC reported. Instead, Anthropic's retreat toward its $83 offer price echoed Seaport Research warnings, covered by CNBC, that its valuation demands much faster revenue growth.

Separately, Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook warned against delaying rate hikes ahead of an expected December increase. Compounding the concerns, President Donald Trump threatened penalties on overseas U.S. data-center builds as new Commerce Department export-licensing rules weighed on chipmakers.

The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

Zooming in on FormFactor

FormFactor’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 86 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 4 days ago when the stock dropped 5.5% on the news that Federal Reserve warnings over debt-fueled AI capital spending and new U.S. export licensing rules clouded the outlook for advanced wafer and tool demand.

Speaking in Milan, Fed Governor Michael S. Barr compared accelerating hyperscaler capital expenditures and over $100 billion in circular equity investments to the 1990s telecom broadband cycle, warning that specialized AI chips could depreciate quickly as newer technologies overtake them and that a sharp reversal could spark "self-reinforcing fire sales."

Adding policy friction, CNBC reported Commerce issued an interim final rule requiring export licenses for advanced chips shipped to Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, and Brazil to stop Chinese firms from leasing Nvidia compute abroad. Foundries and wafer-tool makers monetize aggregate leading-edge silicon volume rather than any single designer's share. When federal policymakers simultaneously highlight potential AI overcapacity and restrict cross-border compute hubs, equipment multiples compress as investors test whether fab expansion plans can outlast an investment slowdown.

FormFactor is up 23.1% since the beginning of the year, but at $72.87 per share, it is still trading 54.4% below its 52-week high of $159.93 from June 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of FormFactor’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $1,710.

data.title: Trump says Democrats facing veto power should work with him
data.description:
By Bo Erickson and Katharine Jackson

US President Donald Trump pledged on Friday to veto legislation passed by Democrats when they take control of Congress in 2027, but said his veto power should be seen as a starting point for lawmakers who want to achieve change.

Speaking at a White House news conference, Trump called the presidential veto "extreme powers," and said his threat to block legislation would cause Democrats to moderate their policies.

"They're going to send things my way, and I'm going to veto them. And then they're going to send more things, and I'm going to veto them," Trump said. "And they could go two years and one month, because that's what we have, and I'm going to veto them."

Trump said Democrats may realize that to avoid his veto, they could work with him to accomplish legislative goals.

"Because of the power of the veto, there's a real possibility that we get a lot of great things done," he said.

Trump said many Democrats had called him to discuss healthcare and immigration reform and pointed to healthcare as an area where lawmakers from different perspectives might meet somewhere in the middle.

"I'm open to great healthcare now, especially on healthcare. I'm open to great healthcare now," he said.

"Can it be what they want? No, but it can be a combination of what we all want, and we could end up with great healthcare in our country."

With the new Congress set to choose its leadership soon, Trump described Senator Chuck Schumer, who is vying to become senate majority leader, and Representative Hakeem Jeffries, who is on the path to becoming the next house speaker, both from New York, as "smart" and expressed willingness to work together.

"If they want to get things done, I want to get things done too," Trump said.

Trump also said Democratic Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa had called him two days ago about the border and he thought they could find a solution.

"She was really nice. It was a very productive call, and she wants to have a strong border. And we'll be able. I think we'll be able to work something out," he said.

data.title: SEC Proposes to Bring Securities Reporting Platform Under Direct Supervision
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

The Securities and Exchange Commission is proposing to restructure the system where securities exchanges report trading data.

The proposal aims to change the Consolidated Audit Trail, which is a centralized database that tracks trading activity across securities exchanges.

The SEC has proposed to rescind Rule 613, which requires securities exchanges to report their trading activity to the CAT. In its place, the SEC proposes to require exchanges to report the same information directly to the SEC or its designee.

The move would bring the CAT under the SEC's direct control.

SEC Chair Paul Atkins has been reviewing the CAT and approving amendments that have reduced its annual operating costs by more than $100 million. Atkins has also permanently eliminated the reporting of personally identifiable information to the CAT.

The proposal addresses concerns about the CAT's funding and would put the database on sustainable footing, Atkins said.

Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com

data.title: FDA must pay legal fees to group that won court fight over COVID vaccine records
data.description:
By Mike Scarcella

A federal judge on Friday awarded more than $571,000 in legal fees to an organization of public health professionals, scientists and others that sued the US Food and Drug ​Administration to obtain COVID-19 vaccine approval records.

US District Judge Mark Pittman in Fort Worth, Texas, said the FDA must pay Public Health and Medical Professionals for Transparency fees for the work of their lawyers at Siri & Glimstad in a public records lawsuit that led to the disclosure of more than 1.8 million records. The judge formally closed the case on Friday.

The lawsuit garnered national attention after the FDA said it would take decades to process the records, drawing a rebuke from ​the judge and an order requiring a much faster timeline.

The ​group sued the FDA in 2021 seeking information the agency relied on to approve the Pfizer-BioNTech coronavirus vaccine. Pfizer ​was not a defendant but participated in the litigation to protect its business information.

“It should not have required over 1,600 hours billed across 22 attorneys and staff for the FDA to do what it should have done from the start — be transparent and release to the public the documents it relied upon to license Pfizer’s COVID-19 vaccine,” the plaintiff's attorneys, Aaron Siri and Elizabeth Brehm, said on Friday.

The FDA did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Pittman in a ruling against the FDA said in 2024 “the COVID-19 pandemic is ​long passed and so has any legitimate reason for concealing from the American people the information relied upon by the government in approving the Pfizer vaccine."

The FDA’s compliance with Pittman’s orders showed “that its initial protestations lacked a reasonable basis,” the plaintiffs said in a court filing. “This is unsurprising, given the federal government is one of the most powerful and well-funded entities on the planet.”

The plaintiff had asked the court to award $854,000 in fees. Some portion of the fee award will be paid to an unidentified outside litigation funder, the plaintiff’s lawyers told the court. Such funders provide financing in exchange for a share ​of a case’s proceeds.

The case is Public Health and Medical Professionals for Transparency v. U.S. Food and Drug Administration, US District Court for the Northern District of Texas, No. 4:21-cv-01058-P.

For plaintiff: ⁠Aaron Siri ​and Elizabeth Brehm of Siri & Glimstad

For defendant: Andrew Freidah of the US ​Justice Department

data.title: Honda recalls 810,592 US vehicles over Takata airbag inflators
data.description:
Honda will recall 810,592 vehicles in the United States to replace Takata airbag inflators that could potentially experience propellant degradation, the automaker said on Friday

The recall covers certain 2012-2013 Honda Civic and CR-V models, 2013 Honda Accord, 2013 Acura ILX, and 2013 Acura RDX vehicles originally sold or registered in 14 US states and territories.

The affected vehicles are equipped with front driver and/or passenger airbag inflators containing a moisture-absorbing desiccant. Honda said long-term monitoring and analysis revealed potential propellant degradation in certain inflators in regions with high temperatures, humidity, and significant temperature fluctuations.

The company said no inflator ruptures, injuries, or fatalities have been reported in connection with the newly recalled inflator types.

Honda will replace the affected inflators free of charge. Mailed notifications to vehicle owners are scheduled to begin in December 2026.

Owners can check their vehicle's recall status through Honda and Acura's recall websites or by calling the company's dedicated recall helpline, Honda said.

data.title: U.S. Approves 879,000 AI Chips To China
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - The U.S. Commerce Department approved the sale of more than 879,000 artificial intelligence chips to Chinese companies, including Alibaba (BABA) and Tencent (0700.HK), through May 2026, according to documents released by the House Foreign Affairs Committee on Thursday.

Some approvals involved companies designated by the U.S. Department of Defense as Chinese Military Companies.

The committee said businesses submitted approximately 3.4 million requests between December and May to sell U.S. made AI chips to China, including products from Nvidia (NVDA) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD). The approvals have raised concerns among lawmakers over the enforcement of export restrictions and potential national security risks.

Both Nvidia and AMD said they comply with U.S. export control regulations. Nvidia said the licensing process involved multiple government agencies and strict conditions, adding that it had since stopped shipping H200 chips to China.

The company reported $2.4 billion in quarterly revenue from licensed chip sales to China, although shipments to the country accounted for less than 1 percent of its data centre revenue in the previous quarter.

The documents also identified license applications involving ByteDance, Baidu (BIDU) and Tesla's Shanghai operations. Lawmakers are seeking tighter restrictions amid concerns that advanced U.S. chips could reach Chinese entities through intermediaries.
